title: Even Odd Tree
statement:
You are given the `root` of a binary tree. Number its levels from the top: the root sits on level 0, the root's children on level 1, their children on level 2, and so on.

Call the tree **Even-Odd** when every level passes its test, where a level is read from left to right:

- An even-numbered level (0, 2, 4, ...) may hold only odd values, and each value must be strictly larger than the one before it.
- An odd-numbered level (1, 3, 5, ...) may hold only even values, and each value must be strictly smaller than the one before it.

Return `true` if the tree is Even-Odd and `false` if any level fails.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

Every rule in this problem is about one level at a time: which parity its values need, and in which direction they must move from left to right. A breadth-first search hands us exactly that, one whole level in left-to-right order. So we walk the tree level by level, compare each value with the previous value on the same level, and stop at the first violation.

## Approach

1. Put `root` alone in `current`, the list of nodes on the level being checked, and set `level = 0`.
2. For each level, decide `evenLevel` and reset `prev`: `0` on an even level (every allowed value is larger) or `Infinity` on an odd level (every allowed value is smaller).
3. Visit the nodes of `current` from left to right. On an even level, an even `val` or one that is not larger than `prev` fails; on an odd level, an odd `val` or one that is not smaller than `prev` fails. Return `false` on failure.
4. Otherwise set `prev = val` and push the node's children into `next`.
5. Move to `next` and increase `level`. When no level is left, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`root = [1,10,4,3,null,7,9,12,8,6,null,null,2]`.

- Level 0 is `[1]`: 1 is odd and larger than `prev = 0`.
- Level 1 is `[10, 4]`: both even, 10 is below `Infinity` and 4 is below 10.
- Level 2 is `[3, 7, 9]`: all odd and rising.
- Level 3 is `[12, 8, 6, 2]`: all even and falling.

No level fails, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is checked and queued once.
- Space: O(w), where w is the widest level held in `current` and `next`.

## Pitfalls

- Reset `prev` at the start of every level. Carrying it over makes `[3,10,8,1]` fail, because 1 would be compared with 8 from the level above.
- The order is strict: equal neighbours, as in `[1,10,10]`, break the rule.
- Neighbours on a level may have different parents; in `[1,10,4,null,7,5]` the 7 under 10 and the 5 under 4 are out of order.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `current` | nodes on the level being checked, left to right |
| `next` | children collected for the following level |
| `level` | index of the current level, starting at 0 |
| `evenLevel` | whether `level` is even (odd values, rising) |
| `prev` | the previous value on this level, or a sentinel at its start |
| `val` | value of the node being checked |

narration.2: Start the breadth-first search with the root as the only node of level 0.
narration.5: Process one whole level per pass until no nodes remain.
narration.6: The children of this level will be gathered here for the next pass.
narration.7: Even levels need odd, rising values; odd levels need even, falling values.
narration.8: Reset prev to a sentinel that any allowed first value beats: 0 when rising, Infinity when falling.
narration.10: Visit this level's nodes from left to right.
narration.12: On an even level, an even value or one not above the previous value breaks the rules.
narration.13: One broken rule is enough to reject the whole tree.
narration.15: On an odd level, an odd value or one not below the previous value breaks the rules.
narration.18: This value passed, so it becomes the one the next node is compared with.
narration.19: Queue the left child first so the next level stays in left-to-right order.
narration.26: The children become the level to check next.
narration.29: Every level passed its test, so the tree is Even-Odd.
